programme: HAND2 and HOXA13, neural-crest/HOX-lineage transcription factors that pattern craniofacial mesenchyme downstream of TWIST1-class regulators, together with SON, a splicing/genome-integrity factor whose loss causes Zhu-Tokita-Takenouchi-Kim (ZTTK) syndrome — three loci recurrently disrupted, either by point mutation (SON) or by segmental deletion/duplication (HAND2, HOXA13 regions), in patients reported with both a calvarial/suture phenotype and intellectual disability.
role_in_a: HAND2 acts in neural-crest-derived craniofacial mesenchyme downstream of Twist1/Dlx5 to pattern jaw and skull elements; HOXA13 sits in the 7p15 region implicated in craniofacial anomalies and in a 7p21.1-p14.3 deletion spanning the TWIST1 locus; SON loss-of-function defines ZTTK syndrome, whose reported spectrum includes craniosynostosis-type skull features.
role_in_b: SON haploinsufficiency is a direct, monogenic cause of intellectual disability as the defining lesion of ZTTK syndrome; HAND2 and HOXA13 lie within chromosomal segments (4q32.1-q35.2 duplication/1q43q44 deletion; 7p15/7p21 deletions) recurrently reported in patients with developmental delay or intellectual disability, generally as part of larger multi-gene rearrangements rather than as isolated lesions.
shared_axis: All three loci are recurrently swept up in structural genomic rearrangements or, for SON, a stand-alone loss-of-function mutation, that produce a combined phenotype because the neural-crest- and progenitor-patterning programmes these genes participate in act during overlapping windows in both cranial skeletogenesis and cortical development.
reasoning: SON's dual role is documented directly and repeatedly in the ZTTK literature, and HAND2/HOXA13 each have at least one report placing the same patient's deletion/duplication in both disease categories, so the pairing is not fabricated. But the three genes have no shared molecular function (splicing factor versus patterning transcription factors), so the account rests on convergent case-report genomics rather than a single documented pathway, and half the concordant factor list (ELF5, LYL1, NR5A1, NR5A2, ZNF354C, ZNF202) has no plausible or retrieved connection to either disease.
support: PMID 22570644 — 7p21.1-p14.3 microdeletion spanning the TWIST1 locus toward the HOXA13 region reported with severe developmental delay; PMID 29177010 — 7p15 deletion encompassing HOXA13 reported with hand-foot-genital syndrome and craniofacial features, concerning both diseases; PMID 39707586 — HAND2 acts downstream of Twist1/Dlx5 in craniofacial jaw patterning; PMID 30410579 — 1q43q44 deletion with 4q32.1q35.2 duplication spanning HAND2 reported with combined craniofacial and neurodevelopmental phenotype, concerning both diseases; PMID 24459084 — 4q duplication spanning HAND2 characterized in two patients with developmental features; PMID 42756707, 42609909, 40636265, 40991760 — ZTTK syndrome case and review reports documenting SON loss-of-function with both craniosynostosis-spectrum skull features and intellectual disability in the same patients.
how_to_falsify: Check whether isolated SON loss-of-function mutations (not accompanied by any HAND2 or HOXA13 co-deletion) reliably produce craniosynostosis-spectrum skull findings in published ZTTK case series; if calvarial/suture anomalies are absent or rare in SON-only cases, the joint phenotype is better explained by contiguous-gene effects in the HAND2/HOXA13 rearrangement cases than by a shared developmental programme, and this account would be wrong.
caveats: The network was estimated from blood expression and projected onto a bone-associated disease term, so no factor here is a direct measurement of cranial suture or brain tissue. Only 15 patient-group comparisons and 2 independent cohort pairs support this pair, a narrow base. IKZF1 and other immune regulators were removed as tissue-generic given the blood substrate, which is why the surviving list skews toward non-immune developmental and syndromic genes; six of the twelve concordant factors (ELF5, LYL1, NR5A1, NR5A2, ZNF354C, ZNF202) carry no defensible connection to either disease and are excluded from this account rather than explained by it.
